questions.q: What did Alan do when the captain showed his face in the open door?
choices: Slammed the door shut and barred it with a bench
Pointed his sword at him and cried "Stand!"
Fired a pistol at him over David's shoulder
Offered him the belt of gold to leave them alone
questions.evidence: "Stand!" cried Alan, and pointed his sword at him

questions.q: What did Alan say was his badge?
choices: The oak
The eagle
The rose
The thistle
questions.evidence: My badge is the oak

questions.q: What did the captain say to David before he left the doorway?
choices: "David, I'll mind this"
"David, you are a brave lad"
"David, come out and you'll be safe"
"David, bring me the gold"
questions.evidence: I'll mind this

questions.q: Why did Alan hold a dirk in his left hand?
choices: In case the men ran in under his sword
Because his right arm had been hurt
So that he could throw it at the captain
To cut the ropes that held the hatch
questions.evidence: in case they should run in under his sword

questions.q: How did David know the crew were getting weapons ready on deck?
choices: Alan saw the flash of swords in the lamplight
Mr. Riach shouted a warning across the deck
He saw them through the window loading their muskets
He heard a clash of steel as a cutlass was dropped
questions.evidence: there came a clash of steel upon the deck

questions.q: Who was the first man to cross blades with Alan in the doorway?
choices: Mr. Shuan
Mr. Riach
The ship's cook
The captain
questions.evidence: saw Mr. Shuan in the doorway, crossing blades with Alan

questions.q: What were the five men carrying when they ran past David's window?
choices: A heavy fishing net to throw over Alan
Long poles with hooks on the ends
A spare yard to use as a battering-ram
Buckets of water to put out a fire
questions.evidence: carrying a spare yard for a battering-ram

questions.q: What did the five men do after David's third shot?
choices: Threw down the yard and ran for it
Broke the door down with the yard
Climbed onto the roof of the round-house
Fired their muskets through the window
questions.evidence: the whole party threw down the yard and ran for it

questions.q: Whom did David think he had "winged" with his first shot?
choices: The captain
Mr. Shuan
A cabin-boy
Mr. Riach
questions.evidence: I told him I had winged one, and thought it was the captain

questions.q: A sailor says, "It was Shuan bauchled it." Using the note in the text, what does "bauchled" mean?
choices: Planned
Bungled
Started
Ordered
questions.evidence: * Bungled.

questions.q: What was the signal for the second attack?
choices: A single call on the sea-pipe
A shout from the captain
The ringing of the ship's bell
A shot fired from the deck
questions.evidence: there came a single call on the sea-pipe, and that was the signal

questions.q: Why didn't David fire at first when the man from the skylight landed?
choices: His pistol was not loaded and he had no time to charge it
Alan had told him never to fire inside the round-house
At the touch of a living man his whole flesh misgave him
He thought the man was a friend who had come to help them
questions.evidence: my whole flesh misgave me

questions.q: What did David do after shooting the two men who came through the skylight?
choices: Sat down and began loading every pistol again as fast as he could
Climbed up through the broken skylight to escape onto the deck
Heard Alan shout for help and ran at the attackers with a cutlass
Hid under the table until the noise of the fighting had died away
questions.evidence: catching up my cutlass, fell on them in flank

questions.q: How does David describe Alan chasing the seamen along the deck?
choices: As a cat chases a mouse
As a hawk chases a sparrow
As a sheep-dog chases sheep
As a wolf chases a deer
questions.evidence: as a sheep-dog chases sheep

questions.q: Where did the beaten seamen go to hide?
choices: Into the ship's boat, which they pushed off
Down into the hold where the cargo was kept
Up the masts and into the rigging of the brig
Into the forecastle, clapping the hatch shut
questions.evidence: we heard them tumble one upon another into the forecastle

questions.q: How did Alan act right after the fight was won?
choices: He sat quietly and prayed for the men who had died
He scolded David for not shooting more of the crew
He began to plan an escape in the ship's small boat
He hugged David, boasted, and made up a Gaelic song
questions.evidence: am I no a bonny fighter?

questions.q: Why does David say Alan's song was "something less than just" to him?
choices: It called David a Whig and an enemy of the clans
It said that David had run away during the battle
It made fun of David for crying like a child after the fight
It praised only Alan's sword, though David did his share
questions.evidence: might have claimed a place in Alan's verses

questions.q: How did David feel once the fighting was over?
choices: So tired that he fell asleep before Alan finished speaking
So horrified by what he had done that he sobbed like a child
So angry at the captain that he wanted to fight again
So proud of himself that he sang along with Alan's song
questions.evidence: I began to sob and cry like any child

questions.q: What land did David see from the round-house door in the morning?
choices: The hills of Skye and the isle of Rum
The rocky coast around Cape Wrath
The city of Edinburgh and its castle
The low sandy shore of the Carolinas
questions.evidence: I saw the great stone hills of Skye on the right hand

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: The captain making peace with Alan and paying him back his gold
The death of Mr. Riach in a storm off the coast of Skye
David and Alan escaping from the brig in a small boat at night
Alan and David fighting off the crew and winning the round-house
questions.evidence: there were Alan and I victorious and unhurt
